items.name: Residential Solar
items.short: Solar power designed around your household.
items.problem: Grid power can be unreliable or costly, and every home has a different roof, orientation and daily energy pattern.
items.application: Homeowners who want dependable power for lighting, appliances, electronics and — where needed — battery backup.
approach: Assess your roof structure, orientation and available space
Review your appliances and daily/seasonal energy use
Design a panel layout and inverter configuration for your site
Size battery storage only where it fits your requirement and budget

faq.q: How long does a residential installation take?
faq.a: Timelines depend on system size and site complexity. We confirm a schedule with you after the site assessment.

faq.q: Do I need to change my roof?
faq.a: In most cases no. Our design team checks your roof structure and orientation on-site and specifies any reinforcement needed before installation.

faq.q: Can I add battery backup later?
faq.a: Many hybrid inverter systems can be expanded with battery storage later. We can design with future expansion in mind if that matters to you.

items.name: Commercial Solar
items.short: Systems sized to your business's load and operating hours.
items.problem: Businesses need power that matches operating hours, equipment loads and cost predictability — without downtime risk.
items.application: Offices, retail, warehouses and light industrial sites looking to manage energy costs and improve power reliability.
approach: Review your load profile, equipment and operating schedule
Assess roof, ground or carport space for the array
Design a system architecture matched to your demand curve
Plan installation around your operating hours to limit disruption

faq.q: Will installation disrupt our operations?
faq.a: We plan installation work around your operating hours where possible and confirm the approach with you before work begins.

faq.q: Can this reduce our exposure to grid outages?
faq.a: A correctly designed hybrid or backup system can maintain power to priority loads during outages. We size this based on your assessment.

faq.q: Do you handle ground-mount as well as rooftop?
faq.a: Yes — we assess your site and recommend roof, ground or carport mounting based on space, structure and shading.

items.name: Agriculture & Irrigation
items.short: Solar water pumping and irrigation for farms.
items.problem: Irrigation and livestock water needs often sit far from grid power, and diesel pumping is costly to run and maintain.
items.application: Farms, boreholes and irrigation schemes needing dependable water pumping without relying on fuel or grid access.
approach: Assess your water source, borehole yield and required flow
Size the solar array and pump to your water demand
Plan storage (tank or reservoir) to buffer non-sunlight hours
Design for your terrain, distances and access for maintenance

faq.q: What determines the pump and array size?
faq.a: Borehole yield, required flow rate, total dynamic head and your daily water demand — all confirmed during the site assessment.

faq.q: Does this work with an existing borehole?
faq.a: In most cases yes. We assess your existing borehole and pump setup to determine what can be reused or needs replacing.

faq.q: Can it also power other equipment on the farm?
faq.a: Yes, we can discuss combining irrigation pumping with broader farm power needs during your consultation.

items.name: Institutional Solar
items.problem: Schools, clinics and hospitality sites need consistent power for critical loads, occupants and equipment, often on a defined budget cycle.
items.application: Schools, healthcare facilities, hospitality properties and other institutions requiring dependable, well-documented systems.
approach: Identify priority loads (medical equipment, refrigeration, lighting, connectivity)
Assess site constraints and any phased-installation needs
Design for reliability and, where required, backup continuity
Document the system for institutional record-keeping and maintenance planning

faq.q: Can systems be installed in phases?
faq.a: Yes, larger institutional projects can often be phased to match budget cycles. We discuss this during design.

faq.q: Do you provide documentation for our records?
faq.a: We can provide system documentation appropriate to your project; specific reporting requirements are confirmed during consultation.

faq.q: How do you handle critical loads like medical refrigeration?
faq.a: We identify priority loads during the assessment and design backup capacity around them specifically.

items.name: Water Pumping
items.problem: Pumping water without grid access or with high fuel costs limits farms, livestock operations and rural sites.
items.application: Boreholes, livestock watering, water transfer and general non-irrigation pumping needs.
approach: Confirm source type, depth and yield
Match pump technology to head and flow requirements
Size the solar array to daily pumping needs
Specify storage to cover variable sunlight hours

faq.q: Submersible or surface pump — which do I need?
faq.a: This depends on your water source. Boreholes typically use submersible pumps; surface sources may use surface pumps. We confirm on-site.

faq.q: What if my water source has variable yield?
faq.a: We factor this into system design and storage sizing so pumping stays within safe extraction limits.

items.name: Solar Water Heating
items.short: Residential, hospitality and institutional hot water.
items.problem: Electric or gas water heating can be a significant recurring cost, especially for high hot-water-use properties.
items.application: Homes, hospitality properties and institutions with consistent hot water demand.
approach: Assess daily hot water demand and usage pattern
Recommend a system type suited to your climate and site
Plan integration with any existing hot water infrastructure
Design for safe, code-appropriate installation

faq.q: Will this fully replace my current water heater?
faq.a: Depending on demand and system size, solar water heating can significantly offset or replace conventional heating. We size this to your actual usage.

faq.q: Does it work well during cloudy periods?
faq.a: System design accounts for typical weather patterns at your location; some systems include backup heating elements for low-sun periods.

items.name: Solar Lighting & Security
items.short: Wall, garden, street and security lighting.
items.problem: Perimeter, pathway and street lighting often needs power in areas without convenient grid access or wiring.
items.application: Residential compounds, commercial premises, institutions and public/street lighting projects.
approach: Map lighting locations and required coverage
Select fixture types suited to the application (wall, garden, street, all-in-one)
Plan mounting, spacing and cabling or standalone unit placement
Specify battery capacity for required overnight run-time

faq.q: Do these lights need separate wiring to a power source?
faq.a: Many solar lighting units are self-contained (panel, battery and light in one fixture), reducing or eliminating the need for wiring runs.

faq.q: How long do they run at night?
faq.a: Run-time depends on battery capacity and daily sunlight — we specify this based on your required coverage hours.

items.name: Backup & Hybrid Energy
items.short: Keep essential loads running through outages.
items.problem: Grid outages can interrupt essential loads — refrigeration, lighting, connectivity, medical or business equipment.
items.application: Any property that needs power continuity through outages, whether solar-connected or as backup to existing supply.
approach: Identify the loads that must stay powered during an outage
Size battery storage and inverter capacity to those loads
Design switchover behaviour appropriate to your site
Integrate with new or existing solar arrays where applicable

faq.q: Can this integrate with my existing solar system?
faq.a: In many cases yes — we assess your existing setup during consultation to confirm compatibility.

faq.q: How long can backup power last?
faq.a: This depends on battery capacity versus your priority load — sized specifically during design, not a fixed figure across all sites.
